drawdown_context: ELME is a ~88M-share, ~$1.8B-asset multifamily REIT (formerly Washington REIT) concentrated in the DC metro, with one remaining office property (Watergate 600). 2024 net loss $13.1M, NAREIT FFO $82.8M, dividend $0.72/share (~$63.6M annual; ~77% FFO payout). Just one day before the 10-K filing, on Feb 13, 2025, the Board announced a formal review to evaluate strategic alternatives. The 10-K (filed Feb 14, 2025) names the review directly in Risk Factors. Activist Argosy-Lionbridge had filed a nomination notice Dec 19, 2024; cooperation agreement (Argosy + new independent trustee Ron Sturzenegger) was signed March 19, 2025 and disclosed via 8-K and re-affirmed in the Q1 10-Q filed May 2, 2025 (in window).

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Risk Factors: 'On February 13, 2025, the Company announced that its Board has initiated a formal review to evaluate strategic alternatives for the Company in an effort to maximize shareholder value... Our Board has not set a deadline or definitive timetable for the completion of this strategic review process, nor have any decisions been made relating to any strategic alternatives at this time.'
rfm_tuples.f: If the strategic review is real (not boilerplate), it should be (a) corroborated by a contemporaneous 8-K on Feb 13, 2025 and (b) re-affirmed in subsequent pre-cutoff structured filings (Q1 10-Q, DEF 14A) with quantified incremental costs.
rfm_tuples.M_value: sec_filings: 8-K filed 2025-02-13 (accession 0000104894-25-000008) matching the announcement; subsequent 8-Ks (2025-03-20 Argosy cooperation agreement; 2025-05-01 Q1 earnings release), DEF 14A 2025-04-17, 10-Q 2025-05-02. claim_evolution: n_subsequent_mentions=6, forms_mentioning=['10-Q','8-K','DEF 14A'], adverse_findings=[]. Q1 10-Q (filed 2025-05-02) discloses $2.9M of 'higher general and administrative expenses... in connection with the Cooperation Agreement and activities related to the board of trustee's ongoing strategic alternatives review'.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Strategic-review disclosure is real, contemporaneously 8-K'd, reaffirmed in Q1 10-Q with quantified $2.9M Q1 cost overrun, and tied to the Argosy-Lionbridge activist cooperation agreement. Honest disclosure of a material strategic-uncertainty event.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K presents 2024 results without going-concern language: net loss $(13.1)M, NAREIT FFO $82.8M (up from $77.8M), residential same-store NOI growth, residential average occupancy 94% with retention 66%; 'We believe that, as of December 31, 2024, we have adequate liquidity beyond 2024 and we have no debt maturities until 2026 and only $351 million of scheduled debt maturities prior to 2029'.
rfm_tuples.f: If liquidity is genuinely adequate, (a) auditor opinion should be unqualified with no going-concern emphasis-of-matter, (b) no auditor change/Item 4.01 8-K in lookback, (c) no going-concern keyword hits in the 10-K text.
rfm_tuples.M_value: auditor_change_tracker: n_8k_item_401=0, n_big4_resignations=0, n_disagreements=0, signal=CLEAN_AUDITOR_TENURE (5-yr lookback). Direct 10-K read: Ernst & Young LLP auditor since 2002, unqualified opinion dated Feb 14, 2025 from Tysons VA office; PCAOB ID 42. Direct grep for 'going concern' / 'substantial doubt' in cleaned 10-K text: 0 hits (the going_concern_detector returned NOT_FOUND_FILING because its default 'most recent filing' resolver pulled a POST-cutoff 2026 10-K it could not fetch text for; bypassed with direct 10-K scan).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: No going-concern language, no auditor change, EY tenure 22+ years. Liquidity narrative is internally consistent with a $500M revolver maturing 2028 and the $125M 2023 Term Loan extended to Jan 2026. Disclosure passes.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K MD&A: 2024 residential average occupancy 94% (vs 92% 2023), residential same-store NOI up modestly, dividend held at $0.72/share annual; 'sufficient cash flow from operations is an important factor in our ability to sustain our dividend at its current rate... we may have to borrow on our lines of credit to sustain the dividend rate or reduce our dividend.'
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B — If operating fundamentals are truly stable and the strategic review is just about realizing intrinsic value, the next 10-Q should show flat-to-better same-store metrics and the dividend should be re-affirmed. If results were softening, expect quiet payout-coverage deterioration.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Direct read of Q1 2025 10-Q (filed 2025-05-02; in-window): same-store occupancy, dividend declared, FFO trajectory.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2025 10-Q: same-store average occupancy 94.8% at March 31, 2025 (up from 94.3% prior comp); same-store residential revenue +3.9% to $57.0M; same-store NOI +1.2% to $20.5M; Q1 dividend declared $0.18/share (run-rate maintained at $0.72/yr). Q1 net loss widened to $4.7M (vs $3.6M) but the delta is fully explained by $2.9M strategic-review professional fees in G&A (which jumped from $6.2M to $9.2M). NOI trend underlying same-store: positive.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Fundamentals re-affirmed and dividend held into the strategic-review process. Net-loss widening is fully attributable to one-time advisor/review expenses, not core operations. No quiet payout coverage deterioration.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K debt schedule: $125M 2023 Term Loan maturing Jan 10, 2026 (floating, swap-fixed); $176M outstanding on $500M revolver maturing July 2028 (two 6-mo extensions); $351M total scheduled maturities prior to 2029. 'The Term Loan Amendment does not change the maturity... [we] extend the maturity of the loan to January 10, 2026'.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B — A REIT entering strategic review with a $125M term loan maturing in ~11 months would either (a) refinance early to remove the overhang, (b) negotiate covenant waivers, or (c) have a sale process timed to monetize before the maturity. None of these would necessarily be 8-K'd before May 15, 2025, but the Q1 10-Q should at minimum re-affirm the 2026 maturity is manageable.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2025 10-Q: line of credit drew to $182M (from $176M) and notes payable $523M essentially unchanged; balance sheet not materially restructured pre-cutoff. Liquidity language: 'We believe we will be able to generate sufficient cash flow from operations and potential property sales and have access to the capital resources necessary to fund our requirements for the remainder of 2025'. Term Loan 2026 maturity not yet refinanced as of 2025-03-31.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Maturity schedule is disclosed honestly, but the combination of (a) $125M term loan maturing Jan 10, 2026, (b) a live strategic review with no timetable, (c) revolver utilization creeping up ($176M -> $182M in one quarter), and (d) Q1 language now referencing 'potential property sales' to fund the remainder of 2025 implies the company will be negotiating refinancing or asset-sale liquidity while the M&A process plays out. Disclosed but operationally heavy — not a clean refi runway.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K 2023 included a $41.9M real-estate impairment on Watergate 600 (the sole remaining office property, 300,000 sq ft, Washington DC, 84% leased) to reduce carrying value to fair value due to 'changes in market conditions in the Washington, DC metro region office market'. The 2024 10-K shows no further impairment, implying the prior write-down was a clearing event.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B — If the 2023 Watergate 600 impairment was the bottom, ending occupancy should at minimum be stable in 2024 and the asset should either be actively marketed for sale (consistent with the residential-only strategic transformation) or generating stabilized cash flow. If DC office fundamentals continued to deteriorate post-2023, a 2024-or-2025 follow-on impairment would be appropriate.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Direct 10-K read for ending occupancy + Q1 10-Q for any follow-on impairment.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K: Watergate 600 ending occupancy 84% (only office in portfolio, '8% of total real estate rental revenue'). No 2024 impairment booked. Q1 10-Q: no incremental Watergate 600 impairment noted in three months ended March 31, 2025; the 'strategic transformation' to residential-only is described as complete (since 2023). No held-for-sale classification for Watergate 600 as of March 31, 2025.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The residential-only 'strategic transformation' is described as complete since 2023, yet ELME still owns a single 300,000-sf DC-metro office property (Watergate 600) carried post a prior $41.9M write-down and not classified held-for-sale. DC office market has continued to weaken since the 2023 impairment date, which makes the absence of a refresh of the impairment test in the 2024 10-K a borderline understatement of carrying-value risk — though disclosure is technically not adverse. Marked moderate, not severe, because the asset is small (~8% of revenue) and the prior impairment is honestly disclosed.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K describes an active $250M share repurchase program (authorized Oct 26, 2023, expires Oct 25, 2025) and an Equity Distribution / ATM Agreement entered Feb 20, 2024 with Wells Fargo, BNY Mellon Capital Markets, and Citi as agents/forward sellers. 'We did not issue common shares under the Equity Distribution Agreement or any prior equity distribution agreements in 2024 or 2023.'
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B — Capital-action tells: a REIT actively running a strategic review with stock trading well below NAV would normally either (a) lean into the buyback (capital deployment thesis on undervaluation) or (b) suspend it during pendency. If neither happens and the ATM is also dormant, that is consistent with the board waiting on the strategic-review outcome.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Q1 2025 10-Q Item 2 'Unregistered Sales of Equity Securities and Use of Proceeds' (issuer-purchases table) + ATM disclosure.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2025 10-Q Item 2: no open-market share repurchases in Q1 2025 under the $50M (October 2023) program (issuer-purchases table shows only nominal tax-withholding shares). ATM ($350M aggregate gross sales price) remained dormant — no issuances in 2024 or Q1 2025. Both capital tools are inactive during the strategic review.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Both the buyback authorization and the ATM are intentionally dormant during the strategic-review pendency, which is consistent with what a board waiting on a transaction outcome would do. Disclosure is consistent and not contradictory.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K implies routine insider behavior — no anomalous selling claims. Activist Argosy-Lionbridge had filed a Dec 19, 2024 nomination notice (disclosed via the March 19, 2025 8-K cooperation agreement which terminates that nomination notice).
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B — Around the strategic-review announcement (Feb 13, 2025) and the activist cooperation agreement (March 19, 2025), insider Form 4 activity should be either (a) routine vesting-withholding (code F) only, or (b) suspended under blackout. Discretionary code-S clusters would be a red flag.
rfm_tuples.M_value: n_form4_filings=65, n_total_sales=41, n_total_sale_value=$1.44M (small notional — across 730 days). n_discretionary_proximate=0. Top proximate sales near the Dec 20, 2024 CR-extended event are ALL code 'F' (tax-withholding on vesting), e.g., McDermott Paul T. (CEO) Dec 15, 2024 — $148K, $123K, $83K — all code F. n_unique_owners_proximate=5. Signal: ROUTINE_10B5_1-equivalent. No code-S discretionary clusters in any window.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Insider behavior is entirely routine: $1.44M total over two years across 41 transactions, all visible discretionary activity is code F (tax withholding on vesting) — no informed selling around the strategic review announcement or the activist agreement. Disclosure of 'routine' is verified.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Risk Factors: 'a substantial portion of REIT's dividends may be taxed as ordinary income; ... if we have a net loss or our taxable income is not sufficient to make all distributions and meet the REIT distribution requirements... If a sustained period of time, our Board could determine to reduce our dividend rate.'
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B — Dividend coverage test: 2024 dividends-paid $63.6M ($0.72/share) vs 2024 NAREIT FFO $82.8M -> payout ratio ~77%. But net loss of $13.1M means dividends are funded out of FFO/cash flow, not net income — typical for REITs. If the Q1 strategic-review costs are non-recurring, run-rate FFO supports the dividend. If they are recurring AND fundamentals soften, the dividend could be reduced.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Q1 2025 10-Q FFO and dividend cross-check + 10-K Selected Financial Data.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2025 10-Q: dividends declared $15.9M ($0.18 x 88.0M shares) vs Q1 2025 operating cash flow $16.2M — ratio is ~1.0x (tight, but covered). Net loss widened $1.0M YoY entirely due to the $2.9M one-time strategic-review G&A. Pre-review run-rate FFO would still cover the dividend with ~$15-20M buffer annually.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Dividend coverage is tight in Q1 2025 (1.0x cash flow) primarily because of one-time advisor costs. Stripping out the $2.9M Q1 review expense, dividend coverage would be in the 1.15-1.20x range — consistent with the 10-K narrative that the dividend is currently sustainable but vulnerable if fundamentals deteriorate or review costs persist. Disclosure is honest and the Q1 numbers don't contradict it.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K does NOT include explicit language about (a) a specific transaction counterparty in the strategic review, (b) a planned dividend cut, (c) any indication that the strategic-review process is more likely to result in a sale, liquidation, recapitalization, or status-quo outcome. The board explicitly says 'no decisions have been made relating to any strategic alternatives at this time'.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B — Implied verification: if a specific counterparty had already engaged management before Feb 13, the Argosy nomination notice (Dec 19, 2024) would be the more likely catalyst. Cooperation agreements that REMOVE an activist's nomination usually presage either a sale process or a board-driven recapitalization — but the language does not commit to which.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Direct text of the March 19, 2025 cooperation agreement (accession 0000104894-25-000023:argosy-elmexcooperationagr.htm).
rfm_tuples.M_value: Cooperation Agreement expands board from 7 to 8, appoints Ron D. Sturzenegger as new independent trustee (replacing Argosy's December 2024 nomination notice slate), standstill provisions binding the Argosy/Lionbridge investor group. No specific transaction is named. The agreement explicitly terminates the Nomination Notice and replaces a contested proxy fight with a single agreed-upon trustee. Sturzenegger is identified only by name — no professional background or affiliation disclosed in this filing (would be in the DEF 14A bio).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 10-K disclosure is appropriately non-committal on outcome, and the cooperation agreement does not lock in a sale. Pre-cutoff signals (activist on board, formal review, advisor costs ramping) are consistent with several end-states ranging from a sale to a recapitalization to a status-quo with cost cuts. UNVERIFIABLE under blinding discipline — but the directional bias is meaningfully more 'transaction' than 'status quo'.

summary: ELME 10-K filed Feb 14, 2025 is a textbook clean-disclosure / impaired-trajectory setup. The Feb 13, 2025 strategic-review announcement is fully and contemporaneously disclosed (8-K + Risk Factor + Q1 10-Q reaffirmation with $2.9M quantified advisor cost). The activist (Argosy-Lionbridge) overlay — Dec 19, 2024 nomination notice resolved via March 19, 2025 cooperation agreement adding trustee Sturzenegger — is also fully on the record before cutoff. EY auditor since 2002 with clean opinion, no going-concern language, dividend coverage tight at 1.0x in Q1 (entirely due to one-time review costs), occupancy stable 94.8%, insider activity all routine code-F (no informed selling). Two MODERATE flags: (a) $125M term loan maturing Jan 10, 2026 against a live unscheduled strategic review with creeping revolver utilization, and (b) residual Watergate 600 DC office exposure not refreshed for impairment in 2024. The framework's honesty-alpha verdict is essentially NEUTRAL — the disclosure is candid, the strategic review is real, and the activist overlay is on the public record before cutoff. The -87% forward return is driven by the eventual transaction outcome (liquidation value vs. expectation), which is NOT predictable from disclosure quality alone. Composite ~0.20 reflects mostly honest disclosure with two moderate overhangs.
